title: Identity completion unit on the strict quotient-stalk cone
statement: Fix $\ell,E,D,k$ as in [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with $\ell\ne D.p$ and $\ell$ invertible on $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $I$ have IntegralComparisonRealizationCoherence (including its reconstruction normalization), and let $I,S$ be compositor data [def-trf-stalk-compositor-tower-data] satisfying the coherent and quotient-compatible laws of [lem-trf-stalk-compositor-tower-realization]. Let $e_v$ be quotient-section-to-stalk tower isomorphisms with normalized finite germ maps [lem-trf-bounded-quotient-stalk-realization]. There exists a natural chain map $a_0:\Gamma(s,-)\to H(T_{\mathrm{id}}(-))$ such that each unshifted projection sends $z$ to $[s,\mathrm{id},\bar z_n]$ and every shifted coordinate is zero. For every good complex $P$ representing a constructible object $N$ by $q:Q(P)\simeq N$, localization of $a_0(P)$, preceded by the canonical sections factor, is exactly $\operatorname{Fib}(q)$ followed by the inverse specified identity unit and the prescribed identity quotient-stalk realization arrow. The meanings of the arrows are fixed by [def-trf-source-section-stalk-cone-data].

proof.text: Use the reconstruction normalization of the coherent comparison system to obtain compatible quotient presentations, and apply the strict completion-unit model. Apply exact point sections, which preserve the products, and the normalized identity germ maps to its zero-homotopy augmentation.

Apply the coherent point-unit normalization and the simultaneous-presentation compatibility to identify the localized augmentation with the identity realization. Naturality of the unit cancels q and q inverse and proves the equation for every presentation.
